name: image.grade
title: Grade (colour-grade stills)
summary: Colour-grade stills before they go into a page: ordered steps (Lab cast removal, white balance, saturation, tone curve, exposure, clarity, tint inside or outside a subject mask, vignette, .cube LUT), light sources kept on request, an optional glow layer, and before/after numbers.
description: Each image goes through `steps` in order. A step changes only what its own fields say, and a step whose strength is 0 changes nothing; the tool has no look of its own. The ops: `cast` moves a colour cast in CIE Lab (D65, sRGB in): it removes a fraction of one side of a* or b* (yellow = +b*, blue = -b*, red = +a*, green = -a*) and leaves pixels on the other side alone. `balance` is a white balance: it adds the same shift to every pixel's a* and b*, so the greys move and saturated colours keep their chroma relative to each other, where `cast` would drain them. The shift is measured from the image's near-neutral midtones as they are when the step runs ((`target_ab` - their mean a*, b*) x `amount`), or given as `shift_ab` for a cut-out layer with no neutral ground of its own: `balance` in the result reports the shift each image got, to hand to its layers. `saturation` multiplies Lab chroma, everywhere or only in a hue range (`rest` sets the multiplier outside it). `curve` is a per-channel tone curve on sRGB values: an S-shaped `contrast` around `pivot`, `gamma`, a `shoulder` that rolls the highlights off softly and `lift` for the blacks. `exposure` scales linear light by 2^ev. `clarity` adds local contrast to L*: value + amount x (value - blur). `tint` blends toward a colour everywhere, inside or outside the subject mask; `grow` and `feather` hold it off the subject's edge. `vignette` darkens (or, negative, lightens) toward the corners. `lut` applies a .cube 3D LUT with trilinear lookup. `protect` on cast, balance and tint keeps the light sources (`lights`) or the subject (`mask`) as they were. The light mask is found in each image as it entered the grade: bright, saturated pixels in a hue range (orange to yellow by default) and the near-white cores touching them, widened by `spread`; `light_mask.write_masks` writes it out to check. `glow` writes a bloom layer of the light pixels on black, for a page to draw additively (mix-blend-mode: screen or plus-lighter) and pulse. Per image the result gives mean L* and mean a*/b* outside the lights, before and after, and beside them the neutrals: `greys_a`, `greys_b` (mean a*, b* of the near-neutral midtones, set by `neutral`) and `greys_pct` (their share of the opaque pixels). `cast_a`/`cast_b` average everything, so a frame of brick and sky reads as a cast when its greys are neutral; the greys are the white balance. With a mask it also gives the mean L* inside and outside the subject and their ratio in dB. The numbers do not replace looking: put the source and the graded image side by side with image.contact-sheet.

images.description: The stills to grade, each with the same steps.

image.description: The still: a PNG, JPEG or WebP workspace path, job:<id>/<output> or pin:<name>. Up to 16 megapixels. Its alpha, if any, is kept in a PNG output.

name.description: Base name of the outputs (<name>.png, <name>-glow.png, <name>-lights.png), without folders. Default: the source file's name without its extension. Names must be unique within the call.

mask.description: The subject's matte (an image.matte output works): white or opaque = subject. Its alpha is used when any pixel is not opaque, otherwise its luminance. A mask of another size is resized to the image (with a warning).

steps.description: The grade, applied in order. Each step is an object with `op` and that op's fields only; the handler names any field the op does not take. No steps: the images are only measured and re-encoded.

op.description: What the step does. cast: axis, amount, protect. balance: amount, target_ab, shift_ab, min_pct, protect. saturation: amount, hue, rest. curve: contrast, pivot, lift, shoulder, gamma. exposure: ev. clarity: amount, radius. tint: amount, color, where, grow, feather, protect. vignette: amount, softness. lut: file, amount.

axis.description: cast (required): the side of the cast to remove: yellow = +b*, blue = -b*, red = +a*, green = -a*. Only pixels on that side change.

amount.description: Strength; its meaning and range depend on the op. cast (required, 0..1): the fraction of that side's a* or b* removed. balance (0..1, default 1): the fraction of the shift applied, measured or explicit; 1 puts the greys on the target. saturation (required, 0..10): the chroma multiplier (inside the hue range when hue is set). clarity (required, -1..4): local contrast added; negative softens. tint (required, 0..1): how far to blend toward the colour. vignette (required, -1..1): darkening at the corners; negative lightens. lut (0..1, default 1): blend between the original and the LUT.

protect.description: cast, balance and tint: what the step leaves as it was. lights: the light mask (lamps, fire, candles, glowing eyes). mask: the subject. none (default): nothing. With mask and an image without one, the step is skipped for that image with a warning. For balance it only limits where the shift lands; the greys are still measured over the whole image.

target_ab.description: balance: [a*, b*] where the image's near-neutral midtones should land. Absent: [0, 0], neutral grey. A target off zero keeps a wanted warmth or coolness, e.g. the greys of an accepted still. Not with shift_ab.

items.description: One CIELAB a* or b* value.

shift_ab.description: balance: an explicit [da, db] added to every pixel's a*, b* (times amount). Nothing is measured, so it works on a cut-out layer with no neutral ground of its own: give it the shift its plate got (`balance[].shift_ab` in that result). Absent: the shift is measured.

items.description: The shift on a* or b*.

min_pct.description: balance: the smallest share of near-neutral midtones (greys_pct, percent of the opaque pixels) at which the measured shift is trusted. An image with less skips the step: it is listed in skipped_steps, with a warning naming the image. Default 0: any grey pixel is trusted, and only an image with none skips. Not with shift_ab.

hue.description: saturation: act only on this hue range of the colour wheel (0 red, 60 yellow, 120 green, 180 cyan, 240 blue, 300 magenta). Full strength within a quarter of the width of the centre, fading to nothing at half the width.

center_deg.description: Centre of the range in degrees.

width_deg.description: Full width of the range in degrees, edge to edge.

rest.description: saturation with hue: the chroma multiplier for every colour outside the range. Default 1 (unchanged).

contrast.description: curve: S-curve strength around the pivot; the slope there is 1 + contrast, and black and white stay put. Negative flattens. Absent: no contrast change.

pivot.description: curve: the sRGB value the contrast curve turns around. Default 0.5 (mid grey).

lift.description: curve: raises black to this value (v = lift + (1 - lift) v); negative crushes, so values below -lift become black. Absent: blacks stay.

shoulder.description: curve: soft highlight roll-off over the top `shoulder` of the range; values above white (after an exposure push) roll into white instead of clipping, and white itself lands at 1 - 0.37 x shoulder. Absent: no roll-off.

gamma.description: curve: midtone power, v^(1/gamma); above 1 brightens the midtones, below 1 darkens them. Absent: unchanged. The curve applies shoulder, then gamma, contrast and lift; gamma or contrast clip values to 0..1 first.

ev.description: exposure (required): stops; linear light is multiplied by 2^ev. Values above white are kept for a later curve shoulder and clipped only at the end.

radius.description: clarity: blur radius (Gaussian sigma) as a fraction of the image width, so it scales with the size. Default 0.02.

color.description: tint: the colour to blend toward, as hex. Default "#000000" (darkening). Blended on sRGB values, like a layer in an image editor.

where.description: tint: where to blend. Default everywhere. outside-mask and inside-mask need the image's mask; an image without one skips the step with a warning.

grow.description: tint: distance (a fraction of the image width) beyond the subject's edge that an outside-mask tint keeps off (and an inside-mask tint reaches). Default 0.

feather.description: tint: distance (a fraction of the image width) over which the tint fades in beyond the grown edge, so no hard or dark halo touches the subject. Default 0.

softness.description: vignette: how far in from the corners it reaches, on a scale where the centre is 0 and the corners 1: it starts at 1 - softness. Default 0.5.

file.description: lut (required): a .cube 3D LUT (LUT_3D_SIZE 2..129, DOMAIN_MIN/DOMAIN_MAX honoured), applied to the sRGB values with trilinear lookup.

light_mask.description: How the light sources are found, from each image as it entered the grade. Used by protect: lights, by glow, and to leave the lights out of the cast numbers. The defaults pick warm light (orange to yellow); check them with write_masks.

hue_min_deg.description: Start of the light hue range (0 red, 30 orange, 60 yellow). A start above the end wraps through 0, e.g. 340 to 20 for reds.

hue_max_deg.description: End of the light hue range in degrees.

min_value.description: Brightness (HSV value, the largest sRGB channel) a coloured pixel needs to count as light.

min_saturation.description: HSV saturation a pixel needs to count as coloured light. Paler pixels can only be cores.

core_value.description: Brightness a near-white pixel needs to count as a light's core (a blown lamp centre); cores count only when they touch the coloured light.

spread.description: Widening, as a fraction of the image width: the mask is full within this distance of the light pixels and fades out over the same distance again. 0 keeps only the pixels themselves.

write_masks.description: Also write <name>-lights.png, the light mask in grey (white = protected), to check what was found.

neutral.description: Which pixels count as near-neutral midtones: what should be grey when the white balance is right. They give greys_a, greys_b and greys_pct in the result, and a balance step measures its shift from them. A cast stronger than max_chroma pushes the greys out of the limit (greys_pct falls toward 0); raise max_chroma to find them.

max_chroma.description: A pixel is near-neutral when its CIELAB chroma, hypot(a*, b*), is below this.

min_l.description: Lower edge of the midtone band in L* (0 black, 100 white); darker pixels are left out, as shadows carry little colour information. Must be below max_l.

max_l.description: Upper edge of the midtone band in L*; brighter pixels are left out, as clipped highlights read neutral whatever the light was.

glow.description: When present, also write <name>-glow.png: the graded colour of the light pixels in linear light, blurred at each radius, averaged, normalised so the brightest channel reaches `strength`, on black. Absent: no glow layer.

radii.description: Blur radii (Gaussian sigma) as fractions of the image width; a few, from tight to wide, give a hot core with a soft halo.

items.description: One radius as a fraction of the width.

strength.description: Level of the brightest channel in linear light after normalising; above 1 clips the brightest part into a wider white core.

format.description: Format of the graded images (<name>.png or <name>.jpg). The glow and light-mask layers are always PNG.

quality.description: JPEG quality, 1 (smallest) to 100 (best). Ignored for PNG.

greys_a.description: Mean a* of the near-neutral midtones (see `neutral`) before the grade; null when no pixel qualifies.

greys_b.description: Mean b* of the near-neutral midtones before the grade; null when no pixel qualifies.

greys_pct.description: Share of the opaque pixels that are near-neutral midtones before the grade, in percent.

greys_a.description: Mean a* of the near-neutral midtones (see `neutral`) after the grade; null when no pixel qualifies.

greys_b.description: Mean b* of the near-neutral midtones after the grade; null when no pixel qualifies.

greys_pct.description: Share of the opaque pixels that are near-neutral midtones after the grade, in percent.

balance.description: One entry per balance step that ran on this image (absent when none did): the shift it applied.

shift_ab.description: [da, db] added to a*, b*, after amount. Give it as shift_ab to balance a layer cut from this image the same way.
